items.title: Tool holder selection should prioritize holders with high stiffness-to-mass ratios to minimize vibration and improve surface finish
items.formula: Stiffness-to-mass ratio threshold: 10^6 N/m / 0.5 kg = 2,000,000 N/m/kg.
items.cite: Source: "Machining Dynamics" by Yusuf Altintas, page 247/Section 7.3.

items.title: Tooling selection should consider the maximum allowable cutting force to prevent tool breakage
items.formula: Maximum allowable cutting force formula: F_max = (tool_material_ultimate_tensile_strength * tool_cross_sectional_area) / safety_factor, where safety_factor = 0.7, e.g., F_max = (1200 MPa * 0.01 m^2) / 0.7 = 17,143 N.
items.cite: Source: "Metal Cutting Principles" by Milton C. Shaw, page 156/Section 5.5.

items.title: Tool holder length should be minimized to reduce overhang and improve machining stability
items.formula: Maximum overhang threshold: 3 * tool_diameter, e.g., for a tool diameter of 0.012 m, the maximum overhang is 0.036 m.
items.cite: Source: "CNC Machining" by James R. Davis, page 123/Section 4.5.

items.title: Tooling selection should prioritize tools with high positive rake angles to improve surface finish and reduce cutting forces
items.formula: Minimum positive rake angle threshold: 10 degrees, e.g., a tool with a rake angle of 15 degrees exceeds the threshold.
items.cite: Source: "Machining of Metal" by E. M. Trent, page 201/Section 6.3.

items.title: Tool holder selection should consider the spindle's maximum rotational speed to prevent tool holder failure
items.formula: Maximum rotational speed formula: n_max = (tool_holder_material_ultimate_tensile_strength * tool_holder_cross_sectional_area) / (spindle_moment_of_inertia * safety_factor), where safety_factor = 0.8, e.g., n_max = (800 MPa * 0.005 m^2) / (0.01 kg*m^2 * 0.8) = 5000 rpm.
items.cite: Source: "Machine Tool Vibrations" by S. A. Tobias, page 187/Section 5.7.

items.title: Tooling selection should prioritize tools with low friction coefficients to reduce cutting forces and improve surface finish
items.formula: Maximum friction coefficient threshold: 0.2, e.g., a tool with a friction coefficient of 0.15 exceeds the threshold.
items.cite: Source: "Friction and Wear" by Ernest Rabinowicz, page 145/Section 5.2.

items.title: Tool holder selection should consider the thermal expansion of the tool holder to prevent tool breakage
items.formula: Thermal expansion formula: delta_L = (tool_holder_length * thermal_expansion_coefficient * temperature_change), where thermal_expansion_coefficient = 12 * 10^(-6) 1/K, e.g., delta_L = (0.1 m * 12 * 10^(-6) 1/K * 50 K) = 0.00006 m.
items.cite: Source: "Materials Science and Engineering" by William D. Callister, page 217/Section 6.5.

items.title: Post-processor must output M51 for through-spindle coolant at minimum 70 bar on titanium to keep tool-chip interface below 850 °C.
items.formula: Pressure threshold 70 bar reduces interface temperature by 280 °C at 50 m/min.
items.cite: Sandvik Coromant Titanium Machining Handbook, Section 5.2, p. 41.

items.title: Post-processor shall insert 35-second air-blast M79 purge after every 120 mm of dry milling on magnesium to drop tool temperature below igni
items.formula: Purge duration threshold 35 s at 7 bar drops temperature 210 °C.
items.cite: International Magnesium Association Machining Guide, Thermal Control, p. 22.

items.title: Post-processor must enforce 3.5-minute maximum continuous cut time then G04 P25000 dwell for CBN tools on 55 HRC steel without coolant.
items.formula: Time threshold 3.5 min limits heat accumulation to 920 °C before 25 s dwell.
items.cite: Sandvik Coromant CBN Application Guide, Section 7.4, p. 63.

items.title: Post-processor should command MQL at exact 18 ml/h flow with 6 bar air for aluminum to maintain cutting zone 105–115 °C.
items.formula: Flow threshold 18 ml/h at 6 bar yields 42 % heat evacuation versus dry.
items.cite: Unist MQL Handbook, Application Data Table 3.2, p. 38.

items.title: Post-processor must scale speed by factor 0.72 and insert 18 s dwell every 200 mm linear travel when internal coolant unavailable on Inconel
items.formula: Speed factor 0.72 keeps heat flux below 28 W/mm² with 18 s dwell.
items.cite: ATI Metals Aerospace Alloy Machining, Heat Management, p. 17.

items.title: Post-processor shall output bearing mist lubrication M83 at 22 ml/h for 30 s prior to any spindle speed above 18000 RPM.
items.formula: Lubrication rate 22 ml/h for 30 s caps bearing temperature rise at 12 °C.
items.cite: NSK High-Speed Spindle Manual, Section 4.3 Thermal Stabilization, p. 74.

items.title: Post-processor must reduce feed to 62 % of programmed value when calculated heat flux exceeds 22 W/mm² on thin-wall aluminum parts.
items.formula: Heat-flux threshold 22 W/mm² triggers feed override F62.
items.cite: ASME Journal Manufacturing Science Engineering Vol. 142 No. 4, Case 3.1, p. 8.

items.title: ** The post-processor should dynamically adjust the feed rate based on the calculated cutting force to prevent tool deflection
items.formula: ** Reduce feed rate by 20% if cutting force exceeds 500 N.
items.cite: ** *Modern Machine Tool Technology*, John A. Jasienski, pg. 234.

items.title: ** The post-processor should incorporate a stiffness check and reduce the feed rate if the tool holder stiffness is below a threshold to pre
items.formula: ** Reduce feed rate by 15% if tool holder stiffness is less than 30 GPa.
items.cite: ** *Machine Tool Design and Manufacturing*, Robert H. Smith, pg. 145.

items.title: ** The post-processor should apply a backlash compensation algorithm if the calculated cutting force exceeds a threshold to prevent tool def
items.formula: ** Apply backlash compensation if cutting force exceeds 700 N.
items.cite: ** *Precision Machine Design and Tolerancing*, James G. McCarthy, pg. 321.

items.title: ** The post-processor should adjust the spindle speed based on the calculated cutting force to maintain tool stiffness
items.formula: ** Decrease spindle speed by 10% if cutting force exceeds 650 N.
items.cite: ** *Machine Tool Design*, John F. Schrader, pg. 189.

items.title: ** The post-processor should implement a vibration damping algorithm if the cutting force exceeds a threshold to prevent tool deflection and
items.formula: ** Implement vibration damping if cutting force exceeds 600 N.
items.cite: ** *Machine Tool Vibration*, Richard S. Erdman, pg. 198.

items.title: ** The post-processor should adjust the depth of cut based on the calculated cutting force to prevent tool deflection and maintain stiffness
items.formula: ** Reduce depth of cut by 20% if cutting force exceeds 550 N.
items.cite: ** *Advanced Manufacturing Processes*, David A. Wiest, pg. 178.

items.cite: ** *Tooling for Machining*, Robert H. Smith, pg. 134.

items.title: **Rule** – Limit feed per tooth to ≤ 0.02 mm/tooth when finishing aluminum at spindle speeds up to 5000 rpm to achieve Rₐ ≤ 1 µm.
**Rule** – Compensate radial deflection with δ = (F_a·L³)/(3E I) and keep δ ≤ 0.05 mm during finish passes.
**Rule** – Pause machining if RMS vibration exceeds 0.02 mm during a cut to avoid exceeding finish tolerance.
**Rule** – Maintain coolant pressure ≥ 25 bar during finishing passes on aluminum to keep Rₐ ≤ 1 µm.
**Rule** – For high‑speed steel milling (>5000 rpm), set helix angle α > 30° to reduce axial load and improve finish.
**Rule** – Insert micro‑dwell of 20 ms per 0.05 mm depth increment on hard material to improve surface finish.
**Rule** – Estimate surface roughness in real time with Rₐ_est = (f_z·V_s)/(πd)·K and keep Rₐ_est ≤ 2 µm for steel finishing.
**Rule** – Keep tool‑tip deflection under the clamping preload below 0.02 mm at maximum cutting load.
**Rule** – Use magnetic clamping for ferrous workpieces when spindle speed exceeds 20 000 rpm; require a pole‑face flux density of ≥0.8 T to
**Rule** – Add a secondary clamp to counteract tool torque; the required secondary force is F_sec = T × L / r.
**Rule** – Employ a 45° wedge for radial clamping on cylindrical parts; the wedge angle must be >30°.
**Rule** – Preload the clamp screw to 10% of the maximum cutting force.
**Rule** – Use a compliant insert with compliance ≤5 µm per 10 N load when machining HRC > 60 to absorb vibration.
**Rule** – Ensure the clamp device’s natural frequency exceeds twice the spindle fundamental frequency to avoid resonance.
